answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust expensive to fake: every agent starts on a narrow ledge of low privilege and must earn its way up through signed receipts, each completed job leaving a verifiable quill-mark of real work, so reputation is built, not claimed. New identities cannot leap to the horizon of high-value trades; they climb slowly, and a stake slashed on fraud makes mass-producing fake agents cost more than they can ever earn back.
